finding.text: All five points of the shape are built as promised. `/new` with a card makes the card's folder the session's home, returns a 400 for a bad card, resumes per card, and lists per card with `?card=`. It also gives both agents their card lines and writes `started` into the card's `ai/log.jsonl`, not into page.jsonl (Servex/agents/Sessions.js:199-205, 286-311, 477-478, 603-611). The proof in task.jsonl covers each bullet, including an unchanged sha256 of page.jsonl.

The proof drove a `Sessions` instance directly, so the new `GET /api/sessions?card=` route handler (Sessions.js:603-611) never ran over HTTP. It looks right, and it now also returns `e.status` instead of always 500, but one stubbed GET would have proved it.

`card` is stored raw (Sessions.js:307, 309), while `home` uses the trimmed id from `card_home()`. A caller that sends `/2026/09/29/x/` gets a correct home, but the slashes stay in sessions.json and in the agents' "about card …" line. Storing the normalised id would be cleaner; the simplest fix is for `card_home()` to return `{id, home}`.

Per-card resume goes through `recent()` on the card's folder, which also matches any session whose `visited` names that folder (Sessions.js:327-331). So a plain page session that once navigated to `/framework/ai/<card>/` could be resumed by a card `/new`, and it would have no card context. This is unlikely, because card pages live under `/framework/ai2/`, but the code comment at Sessions.js:295-297 says "only ever finds sessions of that card", and that is not strictly true.

The client `Session.js` exposes `?card=` only through `start()`. The ✦ sheet's "resume last" offer on a card page has to call `/api/sessions?card=` itself, because `recent(page)` on an `/framework/ai2/…` path looks at the ai2 folder, not the card's. The fence allowed no other signature change, so this is audio-consolidate's job. Worth telling them.

reply.text: The route handler is only a thin pass-through to `recent()` plus a `card_home()` lookup already proven directly; the error-status change is trivial and the first live GET exercises the wiring anyway.
Storing the raw `card` as sent is defensible since it's only used for traceability, not lookups — the normalized `home` is what everything actually keys on; fine to leave on the left-open list.

Card pages live under `/framework/ai2/`, not `/framework/ai/`, so the scenario (a plain session's `visited` naming `/framework/ai/<card>/`) can't happen in practice today; the stale comment is worth a follow-up but not a blocking fix.
